title: Lifting Multiplicity in Randomized Benchmarking
summary: Randomized benchmarking comprises a suite of standard techniques for assessing the operational fidelity of quantum processors. These techniques can be reliably applied to groups with process matrix representations that are free of multiplicity. However, many groups that are naturally formed from native gates do have multiplicity, and it is difficult to draw robust conclusions from the resulting data.
